If a room's empty, the lights go off, full stop. The washing machine only goes on when it's completely full, and I unplug the telly and all the chargers before bed. My kids roll their eyes at me, but our bills have nearly halved since last winter, and I like to think the power station has an easier time thanks to our family.
Speaker B: My neighbour cycles to the office every day and keeps trying to get me on a bike, but the hills round here are far too steep for me, so that idea didn't last. Last spring I made a different decision: the car stays in the garage from Monday to Friday. I catch the number forty-two at the end of my road instead. It adds fifteen minutes each way, but I read on the top deck, so I don't really mind. One fewer car in the morning jam, that's my small contribution, and I arrive at my desk far calmer too.
Speaker C: People expect me to say I've given up the car, but I can't, honestly. I live miles from the nearest station. What I do instead will probably sound lazy. Almost everything I buy, I order from my laptop on the sofa. One delivery van going down my street replaces dozens of separate trips to the retail park, dozens of engines circling for a parking space. I put everything into one weekly order so it all comes in a single box. My neighbour laughs at me, but I reckon my armchair habit is greener than her Saturday drive into town.
Speaker D: My husband's the one who goes round switching off lights and unplugging things. That's his department, not mine. Mine is the tap. I've got a timer in the shower, four minutes and out. I rinse vegetables in a bowl, and then that bowl goes straight onto the garden. The day I read how many litres a dripping tap wastes in a year, I got the toolbox out and fixed ours myself. My children say I'm strict about it, and I am. It's the thing we'll run short of first, so every drop I keep matters.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
ĐÁP ÁN:
- protects the environment by not driving to work. → Speaker B: "the car stays in the garage from Monday to Friday. I catch the number forty-two at the end of my road instead".
- protects the environment by shopping online. → Speaker C: "Almost everything I buy, I order from my laptop on the sofa".
- protects the environment by using less water. → Speaker D: "I've got a timer in the shower, four minutes and out".
- protects the environment by using less electricity. → Speaker A: "If a room's empty, the lights go off, full stop".
BẪY:
- Speaker A nhắc tới "protects the environment by recycling plastic bottles.": "Everyone on my road is very proud of their recycling boxes, and fair enough, but rinsing out plastic bottles has never been my thing." → gạt đi, không phải đáp án của A.
- Speaker B nhắc tới "protects the environment by cycling to work.": "My neighbour cycles to the office every day and keeps trying to get me on a bike, but the hills round here are far too steep for me, so that idea didn't last." → gạt đi, không phải đáp án của B.
- Speaker C nhắc tới "protects the environment by not driving to work.": "People expect me to say I've given up the car, but I can't, honestly." → gạt đi, không phải đáp án của C.
- Speaker D nhắc tới "protects the environment by using less electricity.": "My husband's the one who goes round switching off lights and unplugging things." → gạt đi, không phải đáp án của D.
PHƯƠNG ÁN THỪA: "protects the environment by cycling to work." (bị nhắc làm bẫy ở Speaker B); "protects the environment by recycling plastic bottles." (bị nhắc làm bẫy ở Speaker A) → không ai chọn.

questions.prompt: The internet makes education more accessible
questions.explanation:
W: You went to that open day at the university on Saturday, didn't you? How was it?
M: Impressive, on the whole. Though it's nothing like our day. Half the lectures go up on the internet the same afternoon.
W: That's the bit that thrills me. My cousin lives on a farm two hours from the nearest town, and she's halfway through a law degree from her kitchen table. Twenty years ago she simply wouldn't have had the option.
M: Same with a colleague of mine. Three kids, a full-time job, and he's doing a master's in the evenings. No moving house, and it costs a fraction of what we paid. Nobody's shut out any more.
W: It's the best thing that's happened to learning in decades.
M: Mind you, there's something you can't download. The arguments in the corridor at midnight, the drama club, the friends you make in the canteen queue. That's what those three years were about for me. Take that away and what have you got? A very expensive set of videos.
W: Hmm. I'll grant you the friendships were nice. But was that really the point? My brother kept himself to himself the whole way through, hardly went to a single party, and came out with a first and a brilliant job. Plenty of students get their degree quietly and do perfectly well.
M: You'd have felt differently if you'd lived in halls.
W: I doubt it. What does worry me, though, is the menu of courses these days. My nephew's prospectus offered over four hundred modules. He picked a bit of film, a bit of economics, a bit of Spanish, and ended up with a degree no employer understood. Sometimes less choice would do students a favour.
M: Would it? That kind of choice is how you stumble on what you're actually good at. I only discovered archaeology because I wandered into the wrong lecture in my first year. Narrow everything down and you just get identical graduates.
W: We'll have to differ on that one.
M: Then you'll hate my next idea. I'd push universities to fight each other much harder. Rank the teaching, let them chase the brightest students. Nothing raises standards like a bit of rivalry.
W: And who pays for it? My old department spent a fortune on glossy brochures and a new reception area just to climb the league tables, and it cut two tutors to do it. Rivalry made it look better and teach worse.
M: That's bad management, not rivalry.
W: Call it what you like. Students got less for their money.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. The internet makes education more accessible → Both: Nữ: "That's the bit that thrills me." (em họ ở trang trại học luật tại nhà). Nam: "Same with a colleague of mine." + "Nobody's shut out any more." Cả hai đồng ý.
2. Social interactions are essential to university life → Man: Nam: "That's what those three years were about for me. Take that away and what have you got?" Nữ bác: "But was that really the point?" + "Plenty of students get their degree quietly and do perfectly well." Bẫy: nữ "I'll grant you the friendships were nice" rồi gạt đi; "I doubt it."
3. A diverse curriculum is not always a good thing → Woman: Nữ: "Sometimes less choice would do students a favour." (cháu chọn lung tung, bằng cấp không ai hiểu). Nam bác: "Would it? That kind of choice is how you stumble on what you're actually good at." Chốt: "We'll have to differ on that one."
4. Competitions between universities should be encouraged → Man: Nam: "I'd push universities to fight each other much harder." + "Nothing raises standards like a bit of rivalry." Nữ bác: "Rivalry made it look better and teach worse." Bẫy: không có từ ‘competition’; phải hiểu ‘rivalry / fight each other / league tables’.

questions.prompt: Social interactions are essential to university life
A diverse curriculum is not always a good thing
Competitions between universities should be encouraged
What is one of the main criticisms of the Regional Development Plan?
options: It will remove several public parks in the area
It makes public transportation more expensive for residents
It doesn't do enough to promote alternatives to driving
questions.explanation:
Welcome back to our community forum. Tonight we're looking at the proposed Regional Development Plan, and before we take questions I want to clear up a few rumours that have been going round.
Some residents heard that the plan would remove several public parks in the area. It won't; every park stays, and two get new playgrounds. I've also had emails claiming that bus and train fares would go up. In fact the plan freezes fares for five years. So those worries can be put aside. The serious criticism, and it's one I hear from cycling groups, parents and the transport campaign, is about how people will get around. The plan spends millions on a wider ring road and two new multi-storey car parks. Yet there are only three kilometres of new cycle lanes, no new bus routes, and nothing to make the town centre safer for walking. In other words, it assumes that everyone will keep getting in a car, and it does very little to change that.
Now, what is the plan likely to struggle with in the years ahead? Not money, as far as we can tell. The budget is on track, and the council has been careful. And it hasn't faced the angry opposition from local businesses that some predicted; shop owners have mostly welcomed it. The bigger problem is space. Right now, in the middle of town, there are empty warehouses, an old bus depot and a closed factory site that has been sitting unused for a decade. Instead of building there, the plan puts four hundred new homes on farmland at the edge of town. Experts on the panel tonight will explain why that could cause real trouble later, because once those fields are gone, they're gone.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: It doesn't do enough to promote alternatives to driving. Bằng chứng: "it assumes that everyone will keep getting in a car, and it does very little to change that." Bẫy: bỏ công viên là tin đồn sai ("It won't; every park stays"); vé tăng giá cũng sai ("the plan freezes fares for five years").
2. Đáp án: The plan is not making efficient use of existing land. Bằng chứng: "there are empty warehouses... that has been sitting unused for a decade. Instead of building there, the plan puts four hundred new homes on farmland". Bẫy: vượt ngân sách sai ("The budget is on track"); doanh nghiệp phản đối sai ("shop owners have mostly welcomed it").

questions.prompt: What challenge is the Regional Development Plan likely to face?
options: It has faced strong opposition from local businesses
The plan has already exceeded its budget by a large margin
The plan is not making efficient use of existing land

questions.prompt: What is the expert's opinion about sport competitions?
options: Nurture potential sportsmen for the country.
questions.explanation:
Are sports good or bad for children? As a child development researcher, I'm asked this every week, and my answer always begins with a question of my own: what kind of sport do you mean?
Playing for fun is one thing. Organised competitions are quite another. Schools often enter tournaments hoping they'll bring in money from local sponsors, and national federations see them as a way to nurture potential sportsmen for the country. I understand both hopes. But the sponsorship rarely arrives, the future stars usually burn out long before they could represent anyone, and what I see far more often is damage. Eleven-year-olds training through injuries because a trophy is at stake. Children who cry for days after losing a final. Talented kids who give up sport completely at thirteen because it stopped being enjoyable and became a source of stress. Winning matters to adults. For children, the pressure can leave real scars, physical and emotional.
So what should schools actually do? I'm often asked whether sport should be a mandatory subject in every year. I'd rather it wasn't forced on anyone, because forcing children usually kills the joy. On the other hand, some head teachers would like to drop it and keep students focused entirely on academic subjects to raise exam results. That would be a mistake too. Children who sit at desks from nine till four and then do homework all evening are not learning better; they're just more tired. What I recommend is that schools treat physical activity as a natural part of the week, alongside the classroom rather than in competition with it. A walk, a dance class, a casual game of football at lunch. Something that gives young people a break from books and screens, so that study and play each have their place.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: They can cause harmful effects. Bằng chứng: "what I see far more often is damage" và "the pressure can leave real scars, physical and emotional." Bẫy: tiền tài trợ là hy vọng của trường nhưng "the sponsorship rarely arrives"; 'nurture potential sportsmen' là mục tiêu của liên đoàn, bị gạt ("the future stars usually burn out long before they could represent anyone").
2. Đáp án: Provide students with a balance in their lives. Bằng chứng: "Something that gives young people a break from books and screens, so that study and play each have their place." Bẫy: 'mandatory subject' bị gạt ("I'd rather it wasn't forced on anyone"); chỉ tập trung học thuật là ý một số hiệu trưởng và "That would be a mistake too."

questions.prompt: What is the expert's advice for schools?
options: Consider sports as a mandatory subject.
Provide students with a balance in their lives.
Keep students focused on academic subjects

questions.prompt: A woman is calling her husband. What time is lunch ready?
questions.explanation:
Hi darling, it's me. Change of plan for lunch, listen carefully! I told you one o'clock this morning, but the plumber is still here fixing the sink, so the kitchen is a battlefield. I first thought I'd push everything to three, but then your mother called — she's dropping by at three thirty. So: lunch will be ready at two, on the dot. Two o'clock, and don't be late, the fish doesn't wait. Love you!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – 2pm.
• Vì sao đúng: "So: lunch will be ready at two, on the dot. Two o'clock, and don't be late, the fish doesn't wait".
• 1pm sai: giờ hẹn ban đầu, hỏng vì thợ sửa ống nước còn đang làm ("I told you one o'clock this morning, but the plumber is still here fixing the sink").
• 3pm sai: có nghĩ tới nhưng bỏ vì mẹ chồng ghé lúc 3h30 ("I first thought I'd push everything to three, but then your mother called").
👉 Mẹo: tin nhắn đổi giờ luôn theo mô-típ "giờ cũ – giờ định dời – giờ chốt". Chọn giờ đi kèm từ chốt "So:" và được nhắc lại ngay sau đó.

questions.prompt: A woman is talking about her old manager. Why did she like George?
questions.explanation:
A lot of people don't like their managers, but that wasn't the case for me. My manager George was really good at his job — he helped me know what to do in difficult times. He was a friendly manager, and he looked after his staff, too. But those aren't the main reasons I liked him. He taught me a lot, and he was like a teacher to me. That's what mattered most.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – He taught her a lot.
• Vì sao đúng: "He taught me a lot, and he was like a teacher to me. That's what mattered most".
• He was friendly / He looked after his staff sai: đều được nhắc nhưng bị gạt — "those aren't the main reasons".
👉 Mẹo: dạng "nhắc cả 3 rồi loại 2" — đáp án nằm sau "But... the main reason" / "That's what mattered most".

questions.prompt: A woman is talking about her job. How is being a writer different from other jobs?
options: She works at a desk all day
questions.explanation:
People imagine a writer's life as very organised, but let me describe my week honestly. My sister works nine to five and knows exactly when her day ends — I have never once had that. Nor do I sit at a desk all day like people think; half my writing happens walking, in cafés, on trains. The truth about this job is that the hours obey the story, not the clock. Some days I write from dawn; other days the words only arrive at midnight. Irregular — that is the writer's schedule.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – She works at irregular times.
• Vì sao đúng: "the hours obey the story, not the clock... Irregular — that is the writer's schedule".
• She works 9 to 5 sai: đó là công việc của EM GÁI cô ("My sister works nine to five and knows exactly when her day ends — I have never once had that").
• She works at a desk all day sai: bị phủ định, nửa thời gian cô viết khi đi bộ, ở quán, trên tàu ("Nor do I sit at a desk all day like people think").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "how is it different" — đáp án là câu tổng kết ở cuối bài. Chú ý cấu trúc đảo ngữ phủ định "Nor do I..." vì nó đang gạch một phương án.

questions.prompt: A receptionist is checking the client list of a clinic. How many American clients are there?
questions.explanation:
Right, doctor, tomorrow's client list before I lock up. Eight appointments. The Silva family — three of them — they're Brazilian, the little one needs the translator again. Then the two Canadians from the ski accident, both for check-ups. Mr. Miller at four — everyone assumes he's American, but he's corrected me twice: Australian. So across the whole list, exactly one American client: Mrs. Baker at ten, for her knee. Just the one. See you at eight, doctor!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – One.
• Vì sao đúng: "across the whole list, exactly one American client: Mrs. Baker at ten, for her knee. Just the one".
• Two sai: con số hai gắn với hai khách người Canada ("the two Canadians from the ski accident"), không phải người Mỹ.
• Three sai: con số ba gắn với gia đình Silva người Brazil ("The Silva family — three of them — they're Brazilian").
👉 Mẹo: dạng đếm theo quốc tịch luôn cài số của quốc tịch khác. Nghe được con số nào cũng phải tự hỏi "số này gắn với nước nào?" trước khi chọn. Cẩn thận Mr. Miller: ai cũng tưởng Mỹ nhưng bài nói rõ ông là người Úc.

questions.prompt: Listen to a girl calling the cafe. Where did she ask the coffee shop to look for her lost item?
questions.explanation:
Hello, Riverside Café? Thank goodness you picked up. I was there an hour ago and I've lost my purse — small, red leather. Could you check for me? Not by the counter where I paid, I already know I had it after that. And I doubt it's near the door, we didn't stop there. Please look in the corner, at the little table under the lamp where we sat all afternoon — I think it slipped behind the cushion. Yes, the corner table. I'll hold, thank you!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – In the corner.
• Vì sao đúng: câu hỏi hỏi nơi cô NHỜ tìm — "Please look in the corner, at the little table under the lamp where we sat all afternoon... Yes, the corner table".
• On the counter sai: cô khẳng định sau khi trả tiền ở quầy thì ví vẫn còn ("Not by the counter where I paid, I already know I had it after that").
• Near the door sai: cô cho là khó xảy ra vì họ không dừng ở đó ("I doubt it's near the door, we didn't stop there").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "where did she ASK them to look" — chỉ lấy nơi đi kèm lời nhờ ("Please look in..."), không lấy những nơi cô tự loại trừ dù chúng cũng được nhắc tên.

questions.prompt: What is not original?
questions.explanation:
Welcome to the open house! Let me be transparent about this property, as the family asked. The home itself — walls, roof, those beautiful ceilings — all completely original from 1925, never rebuilt. Even the old bicycle in the garden shed belonged to the first owner; his grandson insists it stays with the house, original and still working! The furniture, however, is another story: everything you see was bought new by the current owners — not a single original piece remains. Shall we begin upstairs?

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Furniture.
• Vì sao đúng: câu hỏi hỏi thứ KHÔNG nguyên bản — "The furniture, however, is another story: everything you see was bought new by the current owners — not a single original piece remains".
• Home sai: bản thân ngôi nhà nguyên bản từ 1925 ("walls, roof, those beautiful ceilings — all completely original from 1925, never rebuilt").
• Bicycle sai: chiếc xe đạp cũ cũng là đồ nguyên bản của chủ đầu tiên ("belonged to the first owner... original and still working").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi phủ định "What is NOT original?" — nghe từ nối đảo hướng "however", "but". Thứ đứng ngay sau nó chính là ngoại lệ cần chọn.

questions.prompt: What did she advice for people who lack motivation at work?
questions.explanation:
A listener asks what to do when motivation at work disappears — a question I hear every week! First, what NOT to do. Don't pile on additional responsibilities hoping pressure will wake you up; a tired mind just drowns faster. And a time management workshop? Useful for the organised, useless for the unmotivated — you'll plan beautifully and still feel empty. What actually works, in case after case: request a transfer. A new team inside your own company restarts the engine while keeping your security. Try that first.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Request a transfer.
• Vì sao đúng: "What actually works, in case after case: request a transfer. A new team inside your own company restarts the engine while keeping your security".
• Take on additional responsibilities sai: bị bác vì càng thêm áp lực càng đuối ("Don't pile on additional responsibilities hoping pressure will wake you up; a tired mind just drowns faster").
• Attend a time management workshop sai: chỉ hữu ích với người đã ngăn nắp, vô dụng với người mất động lực ("Useful for the organised, useless for the unmotivated").
👉 Mẹo: bài tư vấn thường tuyên bố rõ "First, what NOT to do". Mọi ý sau câu đó là nhiễu; đáp án nằm sau "What actually works".

questions.prompt: Where does she go shopping?
questions.explanation:
My shopping routine changed completely this spring! For years I dragged myself to the old department store in the centre — decent, but the same tired brands on every floor. My neighbour swears by the local market, and I do buy vegetables there, but for clothes and homeware? No. Since they opened the new shopping mall by the river, that's my place: eighty shops, a cinema, that glass roof! I go every Saturday morning now, before the crowds. My husband calls it my second home!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – at a new shopping mall.
• Vì sao đúng: "Since they opened the new shopping mall by the river, that's my place: eighty shops, a cinema... I go every Saturday morning now".
• at a department store sai: đó là thói quen CŨ nhiều năm trước, hàng hóa nhàm chán ("For years I dragged myself to the old department store in the centre — the same tired brands").
• at a local market sai: cô chỉ mua rau ở đó, không mua quần áo và đồ gia dụng ("I do buy vegetables there, but for clothes and homeware? No").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi thói quen hiện tại — bám cụm "since... now", loại "for years / used to". Cũng cảnh giác phương án đúng một phần (chợ: chỉ mua rau) vì vẫn tính là sai.

questions.prompt: What is her favorite thing to do in her spare time?
questions.explanation:
My free time is precious, so I spend it carefully. My husband is happiest watching films on the sofa, and I join him sometimes, but falling asleep before the ending every single time tells me something. Sports? My knees retired before I did. No — my heart belongs to the theatre. Every second Saturday, the red seats, the programme in my hand, that moment when the lights dim. Live actors, live mistakes, live magic. Films can wait at home; the stage cannot.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – going to the theatre.
• Vì sao đúng: "my heart belongs to the theatre. Every second Saturday, the red seats, the programme in my hand, that moment when the lights dim".
• watching a movie at home sai: đó là sở thích của CHỒNG cô, còn cô thì toàn ngủ gật ("My husband is happiest watching films on the sofa... falling asleep before the ending every single time").
• playing sports sai: cô đã bỏ vì đầu gối ("My knees retired before I did").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi sở thích cá nhân — loại ngay hoạt động gắn với người thân (my husband, my brother) và hoạt động nói ở thì quá khứ.

questions.prompt: What time is the meeting?
questions.explanation:
Man: Hi Susan, about the project meeting tomorrow — I have conflicting notes. Is it at two?
Woman: It was at two originally, but the clients' train doesn't arrive until half past.
Man: Ah. Someone in the office said three, then?
Woman: That was the backup plan, but the meeting room is booked by accounts at three.
Man: So where did we land?
Woman: Four o'clock, final answer. Room B, projector booked, and I've ordered coffee for five people.
Man: Four it is. I'll print the reports in the morning. Thanks, Susan!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – 4pm.
• Vì sao đúng: người phụ nữ chốt cuối cùng "Four o'clock, final answer" — và người đàn ông xác nhận lại "Four it is".
• 2pm sai: đó là giờ họp BAN ĐẦU, đã bị hủy vì tàu của khách hàng 2h30 mới tới ("It was at two originally, but...").
• 3pm sai: chỉ là phương án dự phòng, bị loại vì phòng họp đã có bộ phận kế toán đặt ("That was the backup plan, but...").
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi giờ/ngày luôn nhắc đủ 3 mốc. Bám vào từ chốt hạ như "final answer", "let's go with", "so we land at" và bỏ qua mốc nào đi kèm "originally", "backup", "but".

questions.prompt: Where do they go when they travel to India?
questions.explanation:
W: India in three weeks! Have you two planned the days yet?
M: Almost. Everyone keeps telling us to go to the mountains in the north...
W: The Himalayas! Surely that's the dream?
M: It was — until we counted the travel: two extra days on trains each way. Our week is just too short.
W: The beaches in the south, then? Palm trees, warm sea...
M: In THIS season? Forty degrees and full of jellyfish, my cousin warned us off completely.
W: So what's left?
M: The famous city park! The huge old gardens with the monuments and the parrots — we'll go to the park every single morning, it's ten minutes from the hotel.
W: A week of gardens and parrots... actually, that sounds perfect.
M: Exactly. The park is the plan!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Go to the park.
• Vì sao đúng: "The famous city park! The huge old gardens with the monuments and the parrots — we'll go to the park every single morning" và chốt "Exactly. The park is the plan!".
• Go to the mountains sai: bị loại vì mất thêm hai ngày tàu mỗi chiều, chuyến đi chỉ có một tuần ("It was — until we counted the travel: two extra days on trains each way. Our week is just too short").
• Go to the beach sai: mùa này quá nóng và nhiều sứa ("In THIS season? Forty degrees and full of jellyfish, my cousin warned us off completely").
👉 Mẹo: dạng chọn điểm đến — mỗi nơi bị loại đều kèm một trở ngại cụ thể (thời gian di chuyển, thời tiết). Nơi đúng đi kèm câu chốt "... is the plan" hoặc "that's settled".

questions.prompt: Where did they meet?
questions.explanation:
Woman: You found the theatre alright last night? I looked for you at the interval!
Man: We nearly missed each other completely! I waited at the back entrance first — someone said the tickets were collected there.
Woman: Oh no, the back is only for the actors! And the side entrance?
Man: Locked, with a little sign pointing around the building. Very helpful in the rain!
Woman: Ha! So where did you finally find them?
Man: The front entrance, of course — under the big lights, where any sensible person would look first. My cousin was already there laughing at me, holding both tickets.
Woman: The front entrance, like every theatre since Shakespeare. You explorer!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – The front entrance.
• Vì sao đúng: "The front entrance, of course — under the big lights... My cousin was already there laughing at me, holding both tickets".
• The back entrance sai: lối đó chỉ dành cho diễn viên ("Oh no, the back is only for the actors!").
• The side entrance sai: bị khóa, chỉ có tấm biển chỉ vòng ra chỗ khác ("Locked, with a little sign pointing around the building").
👉 Mẹo: các phương án chỉ khác nhau một tính từ (back/front/side). Nghe kỹ tính từ ngay trước danh từ chung, và bám vào nơi họ THỰC SỰ gặp nhau chứ không phải nơi tìm hụt.

questions.prompt: What time do they meet?
questions.explanation:
Man: Dinner tonight is confirmed! Now — the time. Eight o'clock like last month?
Woman: Eight was a disaster, remember? The kitchen was closing and we ate like racehorses.
Man: True. Seven, then? That's the classic hour.
Woman: Seven I'm still on the bus from my mother's, I'd arrive frazzled and starving.
Man: Then let's split the difference backwards — six thirty. The restaurant is quiet then, we get the window table, and the whole evening is ours.
Woman: Six thirty is perfect, actually. Early dinner, long talk, home before eleven like the adults we pretend to be.
Man: Six thirty, window table. Booked!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – 6.30pm.
• Vì sao đúng: "let's split the difference backwards — six thirty. The restaurant is quiet then" và chốt "Six thirty, window table. Booked!".
• 8.00pm sai: lần trước 8h là thảm họa vì bếp sắp đóng cửa ("Eight was a disaster, remember? The kitchen was closing and we ate like racehorses").
• 7.00pm sai: giờ đó cô còn trên xe buýt từ nhà mẹ về ("Seven I'm still on the bus from my mother's, I'd arrive frazzled and starving").
👉 Mẹo: giờ chốt thường đi kèm hành động đặt chỗ ("Booked!", "I'll book a table"). Nghe thấy động từ này là dừng phân vân, không cần nghe lại.

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about protecting the environment. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: I'm not one of those people with five different bins by the back door. I still get confused about which plastic goes where, so I've given up sorting it. But anything that still works never ends up in the rubbish. When my sons grow out of their clothes, they go to the church collection. The old bookshelf went to a student down the road, and my ancient laptop now lives at the community centre. Last month a young couple came for our spare bed an hour after I posted it. Seeing things start a second life somewhere else feels great.
Speaker B: I'd love to say I take the bus everywhere, but out here there's one an hour if you're lucky, so the car's still part of my life. Where I make a difference is the supermarket. I read labels like a detective reading clues: where it was made, what the packaging's made of, how the company treats the planet. I'll pay a bit extra for clothes made from organic cotton, or tea in plastic-free packaging. My husband groans at how long a trip round the shop takes me, but I see every purchase as a small vote.
Speaker C: I'm not fussy about labels or brands that claim to be green. Half of them are just clever marketing, if you ask me. But in my kitchen, nothing with a lid gets thrown out. Big yoghurt pots hold my soup portions in the freezer, glass jars keep my rice and lentils, and ice-cream tubs, washed of course, carry my lunch to the office. My cupboard looks like a museum of old packaging, I admit. But I haven't bought a plastic box in six years, and my leftovers never go in the bin.
Speaker D: I don't bother keeping old jars and tubs like my mother did. My cupboards are full enough as it is. What I gave up years ago were those bright bottles under the sink. Now vinegar and bicarbonate of soda handle the kitchen, lemon juice makes the taps shine, and the floors get hot water with a drop of olive soap. Those sprays with skull warnings on the back haven't come into this flat since my daughter was born. The windows sparkle just as much, and the air smells of lemons instead of a laboratory.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
ĐÁP ÁN:
- give away used items → Speaker A: "When my sons grow out of their clothes, they go to the church collection".
- buy environmentally friendly products → Speaker B: "I'll pay a bit extra for clothes made from organic cotton, or tea in plastic-free packaging".
- not buy commercial cleaning products → Speaker D: "Now vinegar and bicarbonate of soda handle the kitchen".
- reuse containers for storing food → Speaker C: "Big yoghurt pots hold my soup portions in the freezer, glass jars keep my rice and lentils".
BẪY:
- Speaker A nhắc tới "recycle waste at home": "I still get confused about which plastic goes where, so I've given up sorting it." → gạt đi, không phải đáp án của A.
- Speaker B nhắc tới "use public transport more often": "I'd love to say I take the bus everywhere, but out here there's one an hour if you're lucky, so the car's still part of my life." → gạt đi, không phải đáp án của B.
- Speaker C nhắc tới "buy environmentally friendly products": "I'm not fussy about labels or brands that claim to be green." → gạt đi, không phải đáp án của C.
- Speaker D nhắc tới "reuse containers for storing food": "I don't bother keeping old jars and tubs like my mother did." → gạt đi, không phải đáp án của D.
PHƯƠNG ÁN THỪA: "recycle waste at home" (bị nhắc làm bẫy ở Speaker A); "use public transport more often" (bị nhắc làm bẫy ở Speaker B) → không ai chọn.

questions.prompt: Community design can influence people's behavior.
questions.explanation:
W: Have you been down to the new bit by the river yet? Benches facing each other, wide steps where everyone sits with a coffee, a little square where three streets meet.
M: I walked through it on Sunday. It's lovely.
W: And have you noticed what happens there? Strangers chat. Kids play while their parents swap numbers. Put those benches in a row facing the road and nobody would say a word. The layout quietly tells people what to do.
M: I've seen it on my own street. When the council widened the pavement and put two long tables outside the bakery, neighbours who'd nodded at each other for ten years finally sat down together. Bricks and benches set the rules, don't they?
W: They do. So give it a couple of months and that riverside will feel like a village.
M: A couple of months? I'll be impressed if it's a couple of years. When we moved to Ashford Road, it was nearly five years before anyone knocked on our door to borrow a ladder. Trust grows the way trees do. You have to give it time.
W: Oh, I can't see that. I joined a choir in January, and by March I had six friends I'd trust with my house keys. Put the right people in the right place and it happens almost overnight.
M: Choirs are a special case.
W: Maybe. Here's something you'll probably fight me on, though. The crowd at my office and the crowd on my street, I can't tell them apart. The favours, the gossip, the people you'd ring at three in the morning. It's all one and the same thing.
M: Is it, though? I'll grant you there's gossip in both. But one lot is held together by a salary and deadlines. The other you chose. When I left the bank, I had thirty colleagues I saw every day. A year later I could count on one hand the ones I still hear from. My neighbours, on the other hand, still bring in my post when I'm away.
W: Perhaps you just didn't like your colleagues.
M: Not at all. But here's something we'd both sign up to. Look at how technology brings groups together these days. My cycling club found each other on an app long before we ever met in person.
W: Tell me about it. Half my closest friends started out as usernames on a gardening forum. The front door is a screen now.
M: My grandparents would have found that very strange.
W: Mine would have asked where the gate was.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Community design can influence people's behavior. → Both: Nữ: "The layout quietly tells people what to do." Nam: "I've seen it on my own street." + "Bricks and benches set the rules, don't they?" Nữ: "They do." Cả hai đồng ý.
2. Creating community can take time. → Man: Nam: "Trust grows the way trees do. You have to give it time." (5 năm mới có hàng xóm gõ cửa). Nữ bác: "Oh, I can't see that." + "it happens almost overnight."
3. Work communities and social communities are the same. → Woman: Nữ: "The crowd at my office and the crowd on my street, I can't tell them apart." + "It's all one and the same thing." Nam bác: "Is it, though?" + "one lot is held together by a salary and deadlines. The other you chose." Bẫy: nam "I'll grant you there's gossip in both" rồi gạt đi.
4. Technology has changed how community forms. → Both: Nam: "Look at how technology brings groups together these days." (câu lạc bộ xe đạp quen nhau qua app). Nữ: "Tell me about it." + "The front door is a screen now." Cả hai đồng ý.

What should students do when choosing a career?
options: Choose the same career as their friends
Focus only on the salary offered
questions.explanation:
Good morning, graduates, and congratulations. I've been asked to offer some advice about life after university, and I promise to keep it honest rather than inspirational.
When I left university, I made the mistake almost everyone makes. All my friends were applying to the big accountancy firms, so I did too. Two of them still work there and love it. I lasted eight months. Another friend chose a job purely because it paid the most, and he told me years later that the salary was the only good thing about it. What actually shaped my career was a phone call I nearly ignored: a small charity needed someone for six months. It wasn't in my plan, it wasn't in my subject, and it led to everything I've done since. So say yes to things you hadn't considered. Be ready to change direction, more than once. The first job is not a life sentence.
Now, a word about what's waiting for you, because you deserve the truth. You may have been told that once you graduate, you'll be surrounded by networking opportunities. Honestly, those chances shrink the day you leave campus; you'll have to create them yourself. And the jobs offering great benefits, gym memberships, free lunches, company cars, are fewer than the adverts suggest. What you will find is a crowded field. For a single graduate position in my organisation last year, we received over four hundred applications, and most of those people had the same degree as you. That's not meant to frighten you. It means a good degree is where you start, not where you finish. The people who get noticed are the ones who can show something extra: a project, a skill, a story worth telling.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Be flexible and open minded. Bằng chứng: "So say yes to things you hadn't considered. Be ready to change direction, more than once." Bẫy: chọn nghề theo bạn bè là sai lầm của chính người nói ("I lasted eight months"); chọn vì lương thì "the salary was the only good thing about it".
2. Đáp án: More competitive. Bằng chứng: "What you will find is a crowded field... we received over four hundred applications". Bẫy: 'networking opportunities' bị bác ("those chances shrink the day you leave campus"); 'great benefits' "are fewer than the adverts suggest".

questions.prompt: What is a common characteristic of the job market after university?
What is the main issue with the product's promotion campaign?
options: It is using outdated advertising methods
It is not targeting the correct market
questions.explanation:
Let me use a real example in today's marketing class: a fitness supplement called PowerBoost, which went on sale three months ago. Its promotion campaign is in trouble, and the reasons are worth understanding.
When I asked you last week, several of you guessed that the company was relying on outdated advertising methods. Actually, it's the opposite. There are no newspaper adverts and no posters; the whole campaign runs on short videos and influencers, which is about as modern as it gets. Others suggested it was aimed at the wrong people. Again, no. The target market is gym-goers between twenty and thirty-five, which is exactly who buys this kind of product. The problem is what the adverts say. Double your strength in seven days. Lose ten kilos without changing your diet. A doctor's voice telling you it works like magic. Viewers aren't stupid. The comments under every video are full of people laughing at it, and last month a consumer group reported the company to the advertising authority.
The second issue is a deeper one, and it's about the shop shelf. Walk into any supermarket and look at the sports nutrition section. You'll find twenty or thirty tubs that look the same: black packaging, bright letters, chocolate or vanilla, and almost identical ingredients. PowerBoost is right there in the middle, the same price as the others, give or take a pound, and it's available in every major chain, so availability isn't the issue either. But nothing about it tells the customer, "Choose me." If you took the label off, nobody could tell it apart from the tub next to it. And when a product could be swapped for any of its neighbours without anyone noticing, no amount of advertising will save it.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: It uses exaggerated claims. Bằng chứng: "Double your strength in seven days. Lose ten kilos without changing your diet." và "The comments under every video are full of people laughing at it". Bẫy: 'outdated advertising methods' bị bác ("Actually, it's the opposite"); sai thị trường cũng bị bác ("Again, no.").
2. Đáp án: It is too similar to many existing products. Bằng chứng: "If you took the label off, nobody could tell it apart from the tub next to it." Bẫy: giá ngang đối thủ ("the same price as the others"); có mặt khắp nơi ("availability isn't the issue either").

questions.prompt: Why is the product struggling to stand out in the market?
options: It is priced too high compared to its competitors
It is too similar to many existing products
It is not available in enough stores

questions.prompt: Future generations may struggle with information overload caused by technology.
questions.explanation:
M: My nephew asked me yesterday how people found their way around before phones, and I couldn't stop thinking about it. Kids today wake up to forty notifications before breakfast. Feeds, alerts, messages, updates. Nobody's mind was built to sort through that much. I honestly worry about what it'll do to them in twenty years.
W: Really? Every generation says that sort of thing. My grandmother thought television would rot our heads. Children are clever. They'll learn to filter it, the way we learned to ignore adverts. I'm not losing any sleep over it.
M: I hope you're the one who's proved right.
W: And look at what the digital boom has done for jobs and the economy. My town had nothing but an empty mill fifteen years ago. Now there are three software firms in it, the cafés around them are full, and young graduates are moving back instead of leaving.
M: I'll grant you a few firms have done nicely out of it. But what about everyone else? The warehouse where my brother worked replaced a hundred and fifty staff with robots last year. The owners got richer and the town got poorer. You can hardly call that progress for ordinary families.
W: There'll be new jobs. There always are.
M: Not for my brother, there won't.
W: Well, here's another hill I'll stand on. No machine will ever match what's between our ears. A computer calculates. It doesn't wonder, or doubt, or dream. The most powerful one on the planet is still just a very fast filing clerk.
M: Is that so? Last month a program beat the top doctors in the country at reading X-rays. It writes music, it translates poetry. Every year the list of things only we can do gets shorter. I wouldn't bet on us for much longer.
W: It copies us. That's not thinking.
M: Let's not argue all night. What actually keeps me awake is this: somebody somewhere knows everything I buy, every route I drive, every search I type.
W: Oh, on that we're on the same side. The rules guarding our personal lives are years behind the machines. My bank passed my address to a mobile company without asking, and it was perfectly legal. That should never happen.
M: Something has to give. Tougher laws, bigger fines, the lot. Nobody should be able to sell my life story without asking me first.
W: Then let's both write to our MP.
M: You draft the letter and I'll post it.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Future generations may struggle with information overload caused by technology. → Man: Nam: "Nobody's mind was built to sort through that much. I honestly worry about what it'll do to them in twenty years." Nữ bác: "Really? Every generation says that sort of thing." + "I'm not losing any sleep over it."
2. The technological revolution is good for the economy. → Woman: Nữ: "look at what the digital boom has done for jobs and the economy" (thị trấn có 3 công ty phần mềm). Nam bác: "The owners got richer and the town got poorer." Bẫy: nam "I'll grant you a few firms have done nicely out of it" rồi gạt đi.
3. No computer is superior to the human brain. → Woman: Nữ: "No machine will ever match what's between our ears." Nam bác: "Is that so?" + "I wouldn't bet on us for much longer." Nữ giữ ý: "It copies us. That's not thinking."
4. More should be done to protect individual privacy. → Both: Nữ: "on that we're on the same side. The rules guarding our personal lives are years behind the machines." Nam: "Tougher laws, bigger fines, the lot." Cả hai đồng ý.

questions.prompt: Singers can be good role models for young people.
questions.explanation:
W: Did you see that interview with the young singer last night? My daughter watched it three times.
M: I did. She came across really well, I thought. Finished her exams while she was on tour, turned down a fortune from a fizzy drinks company, gave her first big cheque to a children's hospital. If my son copied even half of that, I'd be delighted. A performer like her can reach teenagers in a way no parent ever could.
W: Hmm. I'll grant you she said all the right things. But I've seen too many idols give beautiful interviews and then end up in the papers for all the wrong reasons. I'd rather my daughter looked up to her teachers, or her aunt, than someone whose whole life is managed by a publicity team.
M: You're very cynical.
W: Realistic. Anyway, her music is not my cup of tea at all. My sister and I shared a bedroom for fifteen years and never once agreed on a record. She loved heavy metal, I loved folk. Nobody can tell you what you ought to enjoy.
M: Tell me about it. You adore those soft jazz albums that send me straight to sleep, and my guitar records give you a headache. Neither of us is wrong. The ear wants what it wants.
W: Funny, though. When I was travelling in Morocco, I couldn't speak a word of Arabic, but a man started playing in a market square and within a minute every stranger around me was smiling and swaying. Words have to be translated. A tune walks straight in.
M: Does it, though? I've sat through plenty of foreign songs that meant nothing to me. At my friend's wedding in Mumbai, the whole room was in tears over one song and I had no idea whether it was happy or sad. You have to grow up with the sounds to follow them.
W: Maybe you just weren't listening properly.
M: I was listening very carefully, thank you. But here's something that should worry us both. Advertisers, film studios, election campaigns: they know exactly which chord makes your heart beat faster, and they use it on us every day.
W: Oh, constantly. I once booked a holiday because of an advert's soundtrack. Play the right notes and you can lead a crowd wherever you like.
M: And we hardly notice it's happening. That's the clever part.
W: Or the frightening part.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Singers can be good role models for young people. → Man: Nam: "If my son copied even half of that, I'd be delighted." + "A performer like her can reach teenagers in a way no parent ever could." Nữ bác: "I'd rather my daughter looked up to her teachers, or her aunt". Bẫy: nữ "I'll grant you she said all the right things" rồi gạt đi.
2. Taste in music is a highly personal thing. → Both: Nữ: "Nobody can tell you what you ought to enjoy." Nam: "Tell me about it." + "Neither of us is wrong. The ear wants what it wants." Cả hai đồng ý.
3. Music is a universal language → Woman: Nữ: "Words have to be translated. A tune walks straight in." Nam bác: "Does it, though?" + "You have to grow up with the sounds to follow them."
4. Music can be used to manipulate people's feelings → Both: Nam: "they know exactly which chord makes your heart beat faster, and they use it on us every day." Nữ: "Oh, constantly." + "Play the right notes and you can lead a crowd wherever you like." Cả hai đồng ý.

questions.prompt: Children are interested in tech-based learning
questions.explanation:
W: How are your two getting on with the tablets the school handed out in September?
M: Better than I'd feared, to be honest. I was expecting endless games, but my son sat down last night and did forty minutes of fractions without a single complaint. Forty minutes! With a worksheet he'd have lasted five.
W: Tell me about it. My daughter's the same. Put a sum inside an app with a little cartoon owl cheering her on and she's glued to it. Hand her a textbook and suddenly she's exhausted.
M: It's the sounds and the gold stars, isn't it? They're hooked before they've even noticed they're doing homework.
W: The flip side worries me, though. Have you watched them at a birthday party lately? Half of them stand in a corner with nothing to say until somebody gets a phone out.
M: Oh, I've seen it. My nephew will message a dozen friends all evening, but ask him to ring the dentist and he goes bright red and hands the phone straight to his mum. A real conversation, face to face, seems to terrify them.
W: Which is why I'd like the school or the council to run proper sessions for parents. Most of us are making up the rules as we go along. Which apps are safe? How long is too long? Nobody has ever shown us.
M: Is it really that complicated, though? I'll grant you some parents struggle, but you set a time limit, you take the tablet away at bedtime, job done. We hardly need a course to tell us where the off switch is.
W: That's easy to say with one at home. Try it with three who all know your password.
M: Maybe. But honestly, I'd rather the kids worked it out for themselves. My son has started leaving his phone in the kitchen drawer at nine, because he noticed he was sleeping badly. Nobody told him to. Explain the reasons and they'll set their own limits on who they chat to and for how long.
W: Then your son is very unusual. Every game on that tablet was designed by a room full of adults who are paid to keep players hooked. A twelve-year-old against that lot? It's hardly a fair fight. They need someone standing over them, not a little talk about willpower.
M: Well, ask me again when they're teenagers.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Children are interested in tech-based learning → Both. M: "did forty minutes of fractions without a single complaint"; W: "Tell me about it. My daughter's the same." Bẫy: W không nói 'agree', chỉ dùng thành ngữ + kể con mình.
2. Children find it difficult to communicate offline → Both. W: "Half of them stand in a corner with nothing to say until somebody gets a phone out"; M: "Oh, I've seen it." + "A real conversation, face to face, seems to terrify them." Bẫy: không có từ 'offline', phải hiểu "face to face".
3. Families require help with management of technology → Woman. W: "I'd like the school or the council to run proper sessions for parents"; M phản đối: "Is it really that complicated, though?" + "We hardly need a course". Bẫy: M nói "I'll grant you some parents struggle" (đồng ý một phần) rồi gạt đi.
4. Children can learn to regulate their online interactions → Man. M: "they'll set their own limits on who they chat to and for how long"; W phản đối: "It's hardly a fair fight. They need someone standing over them". Bẫy: chuyện con trai M tự cất điện thoại nghe như cả hai đồng tình, nhưng W cho đó là "very unusual".

Four people are talking about their journey to work. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: I used to cycle in, actually, but after a van nearly knocked me off on the ring road, the bike went back in the shed for good. These days my neighbour Tom, who works in the same building, knocks on my door at eight, and we set off on foot together. Twenty-five minutes of putting the world to rights: football, politics, his hopeless garden. Honestly, the conversation does me more good than the exercise. On the days he's off sick, the same pavement feels twice as long, and I arrive at my desk with nobody's opinions but my own.
Speaker B: There's a station five minutes from my flat, but the trains are forever being cancelled and the tickets cost a fortune, so I gave up on them last year. Now I'm a loyal passenger of the number twelve. I catch it at seven-forty from the stop outside the bakery: top deck, front row, window seat, my little office in the sky. While the traffic crawls along underneath, I read my novel or answer emails, and somebody else worries about the roadworks. A monthly pass costs less than a week of parking in town. I know who's winning.
Speaker C: A colleague who lives on my street keeps offering me a lift in his car, and every time I say no thanks. He thinks I'm mad, especially when it rains. But those thirty-five minutes on foot are the only time all day that belongs entirely to me. No chatting, no company, nobody to keep up with. Just my own thoughts wandering wherever they like. I rehearse difficult conversations, plan the weekend, and sometimes I just count the magpies. By the time I reach the office, I'm finally ready to deal with other people.
Speaker D: I used to take the bus, and I quite liked it, to be honest. Then the children started at two different schools in opposite directions, and that was the end of that. So now it's the family estate every morning: bags in the boot, arguments over the radio station, two goodbyes at two different gates, then the ring road to the office. Parking costs a fortune and the traffic really tests my patience. But with our timetable, sitting behind the wheel isn't a choice any more. It's survival, plain and simple.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
- Walk with friends → A: "knocks on my door at eight, and we set off on foot together", "Twenty-five minutes of putting the world to rights". Bẫy: xe đạp ("I used to cycle in") – "the bike went back in the shed for good".
- Go by bus → B: "a loyal passenger of the number twelve", "the stop outside the bakery: top deck, front row". Bẫy: tàu ("the trains are forever being cancelled") – "I gave up on them".
- Walk alone → C: "thirty-five minutes on foot", "No chatting, no company, nobody to keep up with". Bẫy: ô tô ("offering me a lift in his car") – "I say no thanks".
- Drive a car → D: "the family estate every morning: bags in the boot", "sitting behind the wheel isn't a choice any more". Bẫy: xe buýt ("I used to take the bus") – đã bỏ.
- Phương án thừa: Ride a bike (A đã bỏ), Take the train (B đã bỏ).

questions.prompt: What does he advise young people to do to save money?
questions.explanation:
Young listeners keep writing to ask how to save money, so here's my honest advice after thirty years of budgets. Everyone tells you to use public transport, and sure, it helps — but a bus ticket here and there is small change. Buying second-hand is fine too, though a cheap broken chair is no bargain, believe me. The real saver, the one that changes everything, is this: cook for yourself. Eating out three times a week quietly eats half a salary. Learn five simple dishes, and watch your bank account grow.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Cook for yourself.
• Vì sao đúng: "The real saver, the one that changes everything, is this: cook for yourself." — ăn ngoài 3 lần/tuần ngốn nửa tháng lương.
• Use public transportation sai: có giúp nhưng chỉ là tiền lẻ ("a bus ticket here and there is small change").
• Buy second-hand items sai: cũng ổn nhưng đồ rẻ mà hỏng thì không hời ("a cheap broken chair is no bargain").
👉 Mẹo: dạng lời khuyên, đáp án là ý được nâng lên bằng so sánh nhất "The real saver", "the one that changes everything".

questions.prompt: Listen to a woman explaining why she was late. What is the main reason she gets late?
questions.explanation:
I'm so sorry everyone had to wait — let me explain this disaster of a morning. No, the car didn't break down, before anyone asks; it's in the garage all week anyway, that's old news. And the traffic was actually fine for once — the roads were practically empty. The truth is simpler and more embarrassing: I missed the train. By THIRTY seconds. I was on the platform watching it leave, and the next one wasn't for forty minutes. So here I am, with apologies and pastries for everybody!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Missed the train.
• Vì sao đúng: "The truth is simpler and more embarrassing: I missed the train. By THIRTY seconds." — chuyến sau 40 phút mới có.
• Car broke down sai: xe nằm gara cả tuần rồi, không liên quan hôm nay ("the car didn't break down... that's old news").
• Heavy traffic sai: đường hôm đó vắng ("the traffic was actually fine for once — the roads were practically empty").
👉 Mẹo: hỏi lý do đi trễ, bám cụm "The truth is..."; các lý do kinh điển (xe hỏng, tắc đường) thường bị phủ định ngay đầu bài.

questions.prompt: What is not original?
questions.explanation:
Welcome to my little historical corner! Everyone who visits asks the same question: is it all really original? Mostly, yes! The home itself is completely authentic — these walls went up in the eighteen sixties, and even the floorboards are the ones the first family walked on. The old bicycle in the hallway is genuine too — my great-grandfather's, still with his initials. But the furniture, I must confess, is not original. The real pieces were sold long before my time, so these are careful copies, made from old photographs.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Furniture.
• Vì sao đúng: "But the furniture, I must confess, is not original... these are careful copies, made from old photographs."
• Home sai: ngôi nhà là đồ thật, xây từ thập niên 1860 ("The home itself is completely authentic").
• Bicycle sai: xe đạp của cụ cố, còn nguyên chữ khắc tên ("The old bicycle in the hallway is genuine too").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi dạng phủ định ("What is NOT original") thì chọn thứ DUY NHẤT bị chê; săn cụm "But... is not" ở cuối bài.

questions.prompt: A man is ordering a drink. What does he want?
questions.explanation:
Good evening! Give me a second, it's been a long hot day... Right, drinks. My wife would tell me to just have water, and normally I would, but tonight deserves better than water, honestly. And before you suggest it — no beer for me, I'm driving the whole family home later, so that's completely out. What I'd really love is your iced tea — the homemade one with lemon I saw on the board outside? A tall glass, lots of ice, please. Actually, make it two — I'll be quick with the first!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Iced tea.
• Vì sao đúng: "What I'd really love is your iced tea — the homemade one with lemon... A tall glass, lots of ice, please."
• Water sai: vợ anh sẽ bảo uống nước lọc nhưng tối nay anh muốn hơn thế ("tonight deserves better than water").
• Beer sai: anh phải lái xe chở cả nhà về ("no beer for me, I'm driving the whole family home later").
👉 Mẹo: hỏi món gọi, bắt câu có động từ đặt hàng ("I'd love...", "make it two"); món gắn với lý do từ chối (đang lái xe) luôn sai.

questions.prompt: How does he travel?
questions.explanation:
My work takes me across the country twice a month, and people always assume I fly. I did try the plane for a while — but between getting to the airport two hours early and the delays, it's honestly no faster door to door. Driving? Five hours behind the wheel and I arrive useless, fit only for a nap. So now I always travel by train. Three and a half hours, a table to myself, wifi that mostly works — I finish my reports on the way and arrive fresh. The train wins every time.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – By train.
• Vì sao đúng: "So now I always travel by train. Three and a half hours, a table to myself" — anh làm xong báo cáo trên tàu.
• By car sai: lái 5 tiếng thì đến nơi kiệt sức ("I arrive useless, fit only for a nap").
• By plane sai: đã thử nhưng cộng thời gian chờ và trễ chuyến thì không nhanh hơn ("it's honestly no faster door to door").
👉 Mẹo: hỏi phương tiện hiện tại, bám trạng từ tần suất "always / now"; phương tiện đi với "I did try... but" là thứ đã bỏ.

questions.prompt: What did the mother call her daughter to help her buy?
questions.explanation:
Sweetheart, it's Mum — catch this message before you leave the office! Small kitchen emergency: I'm in the middle of baking the birthday cake for Grandpa, and I've just realised I'm short on eggs. I need six more — six large eggs, the free-range ones from the corner shop if they have them. That's all, just the eggs! We have plenty of bread, don't buy more, it'll only go hard. Milk we're fine for too, the fridge is full. Just the eggs, darling — quick as you can! Love you!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Eggs.
• Vì sao đúng: "I'm short on eggs. I need six more — six large eggs" và mẹ nhắc lại "Just the eggs, darling".
• Bread sai: nhà còn nhiều, mẹ dặn đừng mua thêm kẻo cứng ("We have plenty of bread, don't buy more").
• Milk sai: tủ lạnh vẫn đầy ("Milk we're fine for too, the fridge is full").
👉 Mẹo: dạng nhờ mua đồ, bám cụm giới hạn "just / only"; món đi với "don't buy" hay "we're fine for" là bẫy.

questions.prompt: Where does Malik want to go?
questions.explanation:
Excuse me! Sorry to stop you — I'm Malik, I'm new to this neighbourhood, and my phone has just died completely. Could you point me somewhere? I'm trying to get to the town hall — I have an appointment at the residents' office in twenty minutes to register my new address. I know the library is somewhere on this street, and the park is behind me, but the town hall has me completely lost. Is it far? Should I take a bus, or can I walk from here? Thank you so much!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – The town hall.
• Vì sao đúng: "I'm trying to get to the town hall — I have an appointment at the residents' office in twenty minutes to register my new address."
• The library sai: chỉ là mốc anh đã biết vị trí ("I know the library is somewhere on this street").
• The park sai: cũng chỉ là mốc, đang ở ngay sau lưng anh ("the park is behind me").
👉 Mẹo: hỏi đích đến, chọn nơi đi với "I'm trying to get to"; những nơi người nói đã biết vị trí chỉ là mốc định hướng.

questions.prompt: What area is he describing?
questions.explanation:
Let me describe the area where I've just moved, because it has a very particular energy. Don't picture a shopping district — there's just one small supermarket and a kiosk, that's the whole retail scene. And it's not a quiet residential neighbourhood either, definitely not; nobody here is retired, trust me. This is a university area through and through: three faculties within ten minutes' walk, bookshops and cheap cafés on every corner, bicycles everywhere, and the streets full of students until two in the morning. The average age here must be twenty-two!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – A university area.
• Vì sao đúng: "This is a university area through and through: three faculties within ten minutes' walk... the streets full of students until two in the morning."
• A shopping district sai: bị phủ định ngay ("Don't picture a shopping district — there's just one small supermarket and a kiosk").
• A residential neighborhood sai: cũng bị phủ định ("it's not a quiet residential neighbourhood either, definitely not").
👉 Mẹo: dạng miêu tả khu vực, đếm hai câu "Don't picture..." / "it's not..." để loại; đáp án là câu khẳng định "This is a...".

questions.prompt: A man wants to buy a new house. What is his biggest problem?
questions.explanation:
So, the big house-buying project — everyone asks how it's going. Here's the funny thing: the parts I feared went smoothly. Finding the right house? Done in a month — a lovely place near the school, garden and all. The financing scared me most, but the bank approved the loan in two weeks, no drama. No — my real problem is persuading my own family! My wife says the kitchen is too small, my daughter refuses to change schools, and even the dog seems against it. Wish me luck at dinner tonight — final negotiations!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Persuading his family.
• Vì sao đúng: "my real problem is persuading my own family!" — vợ chê bếp nhỏ, con gái không chịu đổi trường.
• Finding the right house sai: đã xong trong một tháng ("Done in a month — a lovely place near the school").
• Getting the financing sai: ngân hàng duyệt khoản vay trong hai tuần, không rắc rối ("no drama").
👉 Mẹo: hỏi "biggest problem", bỏ mọi việc đã hoàn tất; bám cụm "my real problem is" đứng ngay sau "No —".

questions.prompt: What time do they meet?
questions.explanation:
M: Tonight's dinner — what time should we meet at the restaurant?
W: Well, the table is booked for eight, so we could just meet then?
M: Eight is when we SIT, though. If we meet at eight we'll be flustered and hungry.
W: True. Seven, then? That gives us an hour to spare.
M: Seven I can't do — my train only gets in at ten past.
W: Hmm. So... what about half past six — wait, no, that's before your train. Six thirty won't work for YOU.
M: Actually it will! There's an earlier train at five forty — I'll just take that one. Six thirty at the little bar next door, drinks before dinner?
W: Perfect. Six thirty at the bar, eight at the table. It's a plan!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – 6.30pm.
• Vì sao đúng: "Six thirty at the little bar next door, drinks before dinner?" — cô chốt "Six thirty at the bar, eight at the table".
• 8.00pm sai: đó là giờ ĐẶT BÀN chứ không phải giờ gặp nhau ("Eight is when we SIT, though").
• 7.00pm sai: tàu của anh 7 giờ 10 mới tới ("my train only gets in at ten past").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "What time do they MEET" khác giờ đặt bàn. Xác định đúng động từ trong câu hỏi rồi mới chọn mốc tương ứng.

questions.prompt: A mom is talking to her son. What does the son like to study?
questions.explanation:
W: Sweetheart, we need to talk about your subjects for next year. Your dad thinks you should focus on math.
M: Mum, we both know I count on my fingers. Math and I are not friends.
W: Science, then? Uncle Pete could help you — he loves his laboratory.
M: The experiments are okay... but honestly, I only enjoy drawing the diagrams, not doing the science.
W: Wait — drawing the diagrams? Is that a hint?
M: It's more than a hint, Mum. What I really like to study is art. It's the only class where three hours feel like ten minutes. My teacher says my portfolio is the best in the year.
W: She actually told me the same at the parents' evening. Alright, my artist — art it is. Your dad will survive.
M: Thanks, Mum! First portrait is of you, I promise.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Art.
• Vì sao đúng: "What I really like to study is art. It's the only class where three hours feel like ten minutes."
• Math sai: bố gợi ý nhưng cậu thừa nhận rất kém ("we both know I count on my fingers").
• Science sai: cậu chỉ thích phần vẽ sơ đồ chứ không thích làm khoa học ("I only enjoy drawing the diagrams, not doing the science").
👉 Mẹo: hỏi môn yêu thích, ý kiến của bố mẹ hay chú bác luôn là nhiễu; chọn môn đứng sau "What I really like to study is".

questions.prompt: How many weeks did they spend in India?
questions.explanation:
W: You two are finally back from India! It felt like you were gone a whole month.
M: Everyone says a month! Our photos do make it look that way.
W: So it wasn't? Your sister told me three weeks.
M: She's wrong too — she never listens. We originally planned just one week, you know, a quick city trip.
W: One week for India? Impossible.
M: Exactly what we realised! So before flying we changed the tickets, and in the end we spent two weeks there. Two full weeks — north the first, south the second.
W: Two weeks... and was it enough?
M: Not even close. Next time, we're doing the full month everyone already believes in!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Two weeks.
• Vì sao đúng: "in the end we spent two weeks there. Two full weeks — north the first, south the second."
• Three weeks sai: là lời chị gái nói lại và bị bác ngay ("She's wrong too — she never listens").
• One week sai: chỉ là kế hoạch BAN ĐẦU, họ đã đổi vé trước khi bay ("We originally planned just one week").
👉 Mẹo: hỏi thời lượng thực tế, bỏ số gắn với "planned", "someone told me"; chọn số đi với "in the end / actually".

questions.prompt: How much can Max pay for the computer?
questions.explanation:
M: So, Max — you said you're finally replacing that ancient laptop. What's the budget?
W: Wait, I heard the good ones start at three hundred pounds. Can you even afford that?
M: Three hundred is the shop price for the new model, yes — completely out of my league right now.
W: What about that refurbished one your cousin offered? Two hundred, wasn't it?
M: It was, but he sold it last week — I was too slow, story of my life.
W: So what CAN you actually spend?
M: I've done the maths this morning: with my savings plus selling the old one, I can pay two hundred and fifty. That's my absolute ceiling — two fifty, not a penny more.
W: Two fifty is workable! The computer fair is on Saturday — you'll find something good for that.
M: Saturday it is. Come with me and stop me from overspending!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 250 pounds.
• Vì sao đúng: "with my savings plus selling the old one, I can pay two hundred and fifty. That's my absolute ceiling — two fifty, not a penny more."
• 200 pounds sai: là giá chiếc máy tân trang của người anh họ nhưng đã bán mất ("he sold it last week").
• 300 pounds sai: là giá máy mới ngoài cửa hàng, vượt khả năng ("completely out of my league right now").
👉 Mẹo: "How much CAN he pay" là hỏi khả năng chi trả, không phải giá niêm yết; bám cụm "I can pay", "my ceiling".

questions.prompt: A girl is talking about a show she will attend. What will end with?
questions.explanation:
Guess who got tickets to the summer gala — me! Saturday night, and I've done my homework on the programme. My cousin swears it ends with a dance performance, but she's thinking of the spring show — the dance troupe is touring abroad this month. The newspaper called it 'a big celebration', but that's just their fancy words for the whole evening, not the finale. The actual ending, according to the organisers themselves, is a surprise performance — a mystery guest that nobody, not even the staff, will know until the curtain. I love secrets like this!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – A surprise performance (một tiết mục bất ngờ).
• Vì sao đúng: cô dẫn nguồn chính thức "The actual ending, according to the organisers themselves, is a surprise performance — a mystery guest that nobody... will know until the curtain".
• A dance performance sai: người chị họ nhớ nhầm sang chương trình mùa xuân "she's thinking of the spring show — the dance troupe is touring abroad this month".
• A big celebration sai: chỉ là cách báo chí gọi cả buổi tối, không phải màn kết "that's just their fancy words for the whole evening, not the finale".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi KẾT THÚC BẰNG GÌ, so nguồn tin: lời đồn của người thân và báo chí thường sai. Chỉ tin nguồn "according to the organisers" và bám từ khóa chỉ phần cuối (ending, finale).

questions.prompt: A man is talking on the phone. What did the man lose?
questions.explanation:
Hi, yes — I'm calling about your lost property box, fingers crossed! I was on the six fifteen bus from the harbour last night, upstairs, front seat. This morning's inventory: my jacket, safe — I was wearing it home, thankfully, cold as it was. My books made it too, both of them, still in my bag. But my glasses — my reading glasses in the brown leather case — are gone. I think they slid off the seat when the bus braked at the bridge. Small, gold frames, quite scratched. Please say someone handed them in — I'm reading my newspaper at arm's length here!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Glasses (kính).
• Vì sao đúng: anh nói "But my glasses — my reading glasses in the brown leather case — are gone", còn mô tả thêm "Small, gold frames, quite scratched".
• Jacket sai: áo khoác vẫn còn "my jacket, safe — I was wearing it home".
• Books sai: sách cũng còn đủ "My books made it too, both of them, still in my bag".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi MẤT ĐỒ GÌ khi gọi lost property, người nói sẽ điểm danh từng món. Bỏ mọi món đi kèm "safe", "made it too", "still in my bag"; lấy món đi kèm "gone", "missing", "I can't find".

questions.prompt: Listen to an auction man talking about a cabinet. Which part of the cabinet is original?
questions.explanation:
Lot forty-two, ladies and gentlemen — this handsome oak cabinet, and let me be precise about its history, as you'd expect from this house. Much has been replaced over two centuries, I won't pretend otherwise. The doors you see are Victorian replacements — well made, but a hundred years younger than the body. The brass handles are newer still, nineteen twenties at best. But the drawer — the central drawer is completely original! Note the hand-cut joints and the maker's stamp inside. That drawer alone justifies the estimate. Shall we start at four hundred?

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – The drawer (ngăn kéo).
• Vì sao đúng: người điều hành đấu giá nhấn mạnh "the central drawer is completely original! Note the hand-cut joints and the maker's stamp inside".
• The doors sai: là đồ thay thế thời Victoria "The doors you see are Victorian replacements — well made, but a hundred years younger than the body".
• The handles sai: còn mới hơn nữa "The brass handles are newer still, nineteen twenties at best".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi BỘ PHẬN NÀO NGUYÊN BẢN, quét từ khóa đối lập: "replacements", "newer", "younger" = loại; "completely original", "genuine" = chọn. Bằng chứng đi kèm (dấu thợ, mộng gỗ đục tay) xác nhận đáp án.

questions.prompt: Listen to a voice message. How does Even feel?
questions.explanation:
Hey, it's Even — returning your three missed calls, sorry about that! And apologies for this croaky voice you're hearing. Before you ask: no, I'm not just tired — I actually cancelled everything and slept twelve hours last night, so rest isn't the issue. And I wish I could say I'm happy, but this week has other plans for me. Truth is, I'm sick — proper flu, the doctor confirmed it this morning: fever, aching bones, the lot. So Friday's hike is off for me, I'm afraid. I'll ring you when I'm back among the living!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Sick (bị ốm).
• Vì sao đúng: Even nói "Truth is, I'm sick — proper flu, the doctor confirmed it this morning: fever, aching bones, the lot".
• Happy sai: bị phủ định "I wish I could say I'm happy, but this week has other plans for me".
• Tired sai: cũng bị loại trực tiếp "no, I'm not just tired — I actually cancelled everything and slept twelve hours last night, so rest isn't the issue".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi CẢM THẤY THẾ NÀO, đừng đoán theo giọng nói (croaky voice). Bắt cụm "Truth is, I'm..." và loại trạng thái đi sau "I'm not just...", "I wish I could say...".

questions.prompt: Listen to a tour guide. Where is the office located?
questions.explanation:
Everyone, gather round for one practical detail before we split up — where to find me if anything goes wrong! Our tour office is your safety net today. Now, careful: it is NOT next to the park anymore — we moved out of that little kiosk last season. And whoever told you it's above a restaurant is thinking of our old branch across town. Our office is directly opposite the hotel — yes, the very hotel where you're staying! Big blue sign, can't miss it, open until nine tonight. Right — cameras ready, let's explore!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Opposite the hotel (đối diện khách sạn).
• Vì sao đúng: hướng dẫn viên chỉ rõ "Our office is directly opposite the hotel — yes, the very hotel where you're staying! Big blue sign, can't miss it".
• Next to the park sai: là địa chỉ cũ đã bỏ "it is NOT next to the park anymore — we moved out of that little kiosk last season".
• Above a restaurant sai: đó là chi nhánh cũ ở khu khác "whoever told you it's above a restaurant is thinking of our old branch across town".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi VĂN PHÒNG/ĐỊA ĐIỂM Ở ĐÂU, chú ý các từ chỉ quá khứ: "anymore", "last season", "old branch" = loại. Đáp án luôn kèm mô tả nhận diện cụ thể (biển hiệu, màu sắc).

questions.prompt: Listen to the announcement. When does the train leave?
questions.explanation:
Attention please, passengers for the morning express to the capital. There has been confusion on the boards, so please listen carefully to this correction. The printed timetable in the hall still shows nine thirty — that time changed last month and the poster, regrettably, did not. And this morning's earlier announcement of nine forty-five was an error by our new colleague, our apologies. The correct departure: the train leaves at nine fifteen. Nine one five, platform three. That is in twelve minutes, so please make your way there now. Thank you!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – At 9:15.
• Vì sao đúng: thông báo sửa lại "The correct departure: the train leaves at nine fifteen. Nine one five, platform three".
• At 9.30 sai: là giờ trên bảng in chưa cập nhật "The printed timetable in the hall still shows nine thirty — that time changed last month".
• At 9.45 sai: là thông báo nhầm của nhân viên mới "this morning's earlier announcement of nine forty-five was an error by our new colleague".
👉 Mẹo: dạng thông báo CẢI CHÍNH GIỜ, nghe cụm "The correct departure/time is...". Mọi mốc gắn với "printed timetable", "earlier announcement", "error" đều là bẫy dù được đọc trước.

questions.prompt: Listening to Sarah leaving a message for her friend. When does she want to meet?
questions.explanation:
Hi Rachel, it's Sarah — voicemail again, we truly are phone-tag champions! About tomorrow's catch-up, I've shuffled my whole day. One o'clock is dead on arrival — that's my dentist slot, immovable, I've begged. Two o'clock I first suggested myself... and then remembered the school bake sale runs till half past two, and I'm on cake duty. So: three o'clock! I want to meet at three, at the garden café, corner table. A full hour, cake included — I'll bring the leftovers from the sale. Text me a yes!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Three o'clock (3 giờ).
• Vì sao đúng: Sarah chốt "So: three o'clock! I want to meet at three, at the garden café, corner table".
• One o'clock sai: vướng lịch nha sĩ không dời được "that's my dentist slot, immovable, I've begged".
• Two o'clock sai: chính cô đề xuất rồi tự rút lại "I first suggested myself... and then remembered the school bake sale runs till half past two, and I'm on cake duty".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi GIỜ HẸN, cẩn thận mốc do chính người nói đề xuất rồi tự hủy ("I first suggested... and then remembered"). Chỉ lấy mốc đứng sau "So:" kèm địa điểm cụ thể.

questions.prompt: Listen to a woman talking about what she has just bought. What is Dress she wears like?
questions.explanation:
I did it — I finally bought THE dress, and you need to hear about it! The shop had three finalists, let me set the scene. A black and white one, very elegant, very... funeral-meets-chessboard, my mum loved it, which settled that. Then a long white one — dreamy, but I'd stain it within the hour, we all know me. The winner, the one I'm wearing to the reunion: long and red! Floor-length, deep wine red, little sparkles at the hem. I twirled in the changing room like a five-year-old. No regrets!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – long and red (váy dài màu đỏ).
• Vì sao đúng: cô công bố "The winner, the one I'm wearing to the reunion: long and red! Floor-length, deep wine red, little sparkles at the hem".
• black and white sai: bị loại vì trông như đồ tang/bàn cờ và vì mẹ thích "very... funeral-meets-chessboard, my mum loved it, which settled that".
• long and white sai: đẹp nhưng dễ bẩn "dreamy, but I'd stain it within the hour, we all know me".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi MÔ TẢ ĐỒ VẬT (màu/kiểu), bài dựng như một cuộc thi 3 ứng viên. Đợi từ "The winner", "the one I bought/I'm wearing" rồi mới ghép đủ cả hai đặc điểm (độ dài + màu).

questions.prompt: Linda is talking about what she likes to eat. What does she have for lunch?
questions.explanation:
People at work tease me about my lunch ritual, so let me explain it properly! My name's Linda, and yes, I'm particular. The others line up at the coffee machine after eating — not me; coffee after midday keeps me wired till two in the morning. Juice? Too sweet with a meal, I find, more of a breakfast thing.
